import numpy as np


def verify_draft(tokens, draft_probabilities, target_probabilities, *, seed=0):
    """Verify K proposed tokens using q(K,V) and p(K+1,V).

    p[i] must be conditioned on the prefix plus the first i proposals. The last
    row supplies the bonus token if every proposal is accepted. Return emitted
    tokens and accepted count. On rejection, stop: later rows have stale prefixes.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    q = np.asarray(draft_probabilities, dtype=float)
    p = np.asarray(target_probabilities, dtype=float)
    tokens = np.asarray(tokens, dtype=int)
    if q.ndim != 2 or p.shape != (len(q) + 1, q.shape[1]) or tokens.shape != (len(q),):
        raise ValueError("expected q(K,V), p(K+1,V), and K proposals")
    for probabilities in (p, q):
        if (
            not np.isfinite(probabilities).all()
            or np.any(probabilities < 0)
            or not np.allclose(probabilities.sum(-1), 1)
        ):
            raise ValueError("rows must be normalized probability distributions")
    if np.any((tokens < 0) | (tokens >= q.shape[1])):
        raise ValueError("proposal outside vocabulary")
    output = []
    for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
        if q[index, token] <= 0:
            raise ValueError("a proposal must have positive draft probability")
        if rng.random() < min(1.0, p[index, token] / q[index, token]):
            output.append(int(token))
            continue
        residual = np.maximum(p[index] - q[index], 0)
        residual /= residual.sum()
        output.append(int(rng.choice(len(residual), p=residual)))
        return output, index
    output.append(int(rng.choice(p.shape[1], p=p[-1])))
    return output, len(tokens)

**The draft model proposes; the target model remains authoritative.** A small model can generate several candidate tokens cheaply. A larger target model evaluates that block in parallel, accepting suitable proposals and correcting others. The aim is to save expensive serial target steps while preserving the target model's output distribution under the exact sampling algorithm. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192)

**Why “accept if it looks likely” is insufficient.** Suppose a two-token vocabulary has target probabilities $p=(0.8,0.2)$ and draft probabilities $q=(0.5,0.5)$. Accepting every draft token would produce 50/50 outputs rather than the required 80/20. The acceptance rule must compensate for how often the draft proposes each option.

For token A, acceptance is $\min(1,0.8/0.5)=1$. For token B, it is $\min(1,0.2/0.5)=0.4$. Accepted A mass is $0.5\times1=0.5$; accepted B mass is $0.5\times0.4=0.2$. The remaining rejection probability is 0.3. All positive residual mass $\max(p-q,0)$ lies on A, so every rejection resamples A. Final probabilities are therefore $(0.8,0.2)$ exactly.

**Extend this one-token argument carefully.** Each probability in a draft block is conditional on the prefix accepted so far. Once a proposal is rejected and replaced, subsequent target rows computed for the old draft prefix are no longer valid. Stop that verification block and restart from the corrected prefix. If every proposal is accepted, the target's extra final row can supply a bonus token.

**What determines speed.** Acceptance rate, draft cost, verification overhead, and serving batch size all matter. A draft that rarely agrees can waste work, and high-throughput batching can reduce the benefit. Test output frequencies on a tiny known distribution and prefix consistency before reporting speedups. Exactness refers to the specified target sampling distribution; vocabulary mismatches or inconsistent temperature/filtering rules break that claim.

**Technical details and references.**

Accept draft token x with min(1,p(x)/q(x)). On rejection, sample from normalized max(p−q,0), then stop verifying that block because later target rows used the rejected prefix. If all K proposals pass, sample a bonus token from the target distribution at the full prefix. The accepted contribution min(p,q) plus the residual max(p−q,0) recovers p. Identical tokenizer/vocabulary and correctly conditioned probabilities are necessary.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For one draft draw, accepted probability mass at token $x$ is $q(x)\min(1,p(x)/q(x))=\min(p(x),q(x))$. The residual mass is $(p(x)-q(x))_+$. Their sum is exactly $p(x)$, establishing correctness when the proposal and target probabilities correspond to the same prefix and vocabulary. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://jaykmody.com/blog/speculative-sampling/) and [2](https://research.google/blog/looking-back-at-speculative-decoding/).
